old_problem: The copied DeepSeek command selects SMBIOS Type 18 while this exact row explicitly names Type 12 and checks its Count. A separate same-code row 1935 owns Type 18. The prior review treated this as an unresolved type choice even though the row/variant identity and DMTF structure definitions provide a non-destructive resolution.
disposition_reason: Resolve Pending and Source Conflict. ED-02/ED-19 bind the exact row/variant: row 1933 remains Type 12, while row 1935 independently remains Type 18. DMTF defines Type 12 as System Configuration Options containing a Count followed by that many strings; therefore complete `dmidecode --type 12` evidence directly matches Items and Procedure. The Type 18 command is removed. Expected option strings, multiplicity, reboot command and timing are fail-closed Project Configuration. Logs are preserved rather than cleared.
decision_basis: The exact XLSX row 1933, same-row tests.json/DeepSeek, GPT V2, historical record, same-code row 1935 and ED-01 through ED-30 were read. The actual next queue row was directly opened as Functionality 1935 / Wistron-BIOS-00465-V003 / a7c3fb9231a32e9d.
DMTF SMBIOS defines Type 12 as System Configuration Options with a Count field and a set of configuration-option strings; those fields match this row's title and explicit Count check.
Row 1935 is a separate Type 18 32-Bit Memory Error Information variant using the same code. Its existence confirms Type 18 coverage must not overwrite or satisfy row 1933.
Collection must retain complete raw structure(s), handles, Count and every string; grep, stderr suppression or empty output cannot pass.
One approved warm reboot requires same-target Boot ID and OS Ready proof. Pre-existing dmesg/syslog/SEL are preserved because clearing destroys relevant evidence.
No dmidecode, SSH, reboot, log-clear, firmware, SMBIOS or DUT action was performed.

test_case.test_name: SMBIOS Type 12 configuration-option count and string persistence across reboot
test_case.purpose: Verify every SMBIOS Type 12 System Configuration Options structure has the Project-approved Count and ordered/normalized option strings before and after one approved warm reboot, without cross-credit from the separate Type 18 variant.
required_package: Exact SUT/board/BIOS/SMBIOS identity and versioned recipe listing expected Type 12 structures, Count and option strings including order/normalization/duplicate policy
Validated dmidecode and complete Type 12 parser preserving handles, raw strings, stdout/stderr/status and protected sensitive values
Secure authenticated host access and protected evidence/redaction policy
Approved OS warm-reboot command, workload window, Boot ID/OS Ready timeout and independent console/BMC recovery
Preserved pre/post dmesg/syslog/SEL baseline and explicit same-code Type 18 variant separation
test_case.test_command: READ-ONLY COLLECTION AROUND ONE APPROVED REBOOT; DO NOT EXECUTE DURING REVIEW. Bind the exact target and capture BIOS/SMBIOS identity, Boot ID and preserved logs. Run authenticated privileged `dmidecode --type 12` without grep or stderr suppression; save full raw output/status and parse each handle's Count and every option string against the approved recipe. After point-of-action reboot approval, issue the approved OS warm reboot once, prove the same target changes Boot ID and reaches OS Ready, then repeat and compare complete Type 12 semantics and logs. Do not run Type 18 as this row, clear logs, expose credentials, modify firmware/SMBIOS or automatically retry.
test_case.expected_result: Every required Type 12 structure is present exactly as allowed, Count equals the number of decoded option strings and each value matches the recipe before reboot; after the same SUT returns to OS Ready, the complete Type 12 set remains semantically identical and correct with no unexplained platform-health regression.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires exact identity, successful complete pre/post Type 12 collection, expected structure multiplicity, Count/string correctness, approved Boot ID-changing warm reboot, OS Ready and persistent semantics. FAIL on missing/extra/malformed structure, Count/string mismatch, truncation, command error, unexpected post-reboot change or health failure. NOT READY applies when recipe, access, reboot approval or recovery is absent. Type 18 output, empty/filtered output or cleared logs cannot PASS; end user owns verdict.
safety_gate: Collection is read-only; do not modify BIOS, SMBIOS, recipe, firmware or device state.
Preserve logs and complete raw output; never clear dmesg, syslog or SEL or suppress errors.
Use secure verified access and protect configuration strings; never expose passwords or disable host verification.
Require explicit reboot/workload approval and independent recovery; do not cold/DC/AC cycle or automatically retry.
expected_evidence: Exact row/variant plus separate same-code Type 18 identity, target/BIOS/SMBIOS/dmidecode/parser identity and recipe
Complete pre/post Type 12 stdout/stderr/status, handles, Count values, all strings and semantic diffs
Approved reboot command/timeline, old/new Boot IDs, same-target proof and OS Ready
Preserved pre/post platform logs and health plus no-Type18-substitution/no-clear/no-write/no-retry audit
Protected evidence hashes, workload restore and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: If reboot fails, retain the first timeline/logs and use only the approved console/BMC boot-recovery runbook; do not automatically reboot again. If Type 12 is absent, malformed or changed, preserve complete SMBIOS tables and firmware identity, make no BIOS/SMBIOS edit and escalate to the BIOS/platform owner. Type 18 may be reviewed only under its independent row and cannot repair this result.
